coverage.where: printcheck, printcheckb, PDFs, listing 'Good to know'
coverage.note: True-size pages with a 0.5 in safe area and a mirrored 0.375 in binding margin (measured), no edge tabs. Print check is on pages 3 to 4. The A4 version has 2 holes, the Letter version 3. The listing says Letter and A4 only, no A5 or Classic, and that Letter fits Big Happy Planner discs and 3-ring binders.

Every page type shares one layout. Dates are consistent with the calendar and lines are crisp vector strokes. The check-tech file reports no overflow and 1743 of 1743 links present. Photos are crops of the built pages. The week numbering scheme is non-ISO; see visual issues.

The listing states the dated range Mon Oct 26, 2026 to Sun Jan 2, 2028, Monday start, 1 undated spare week, no daily pages, Letter and A4 only, and 164 pages, which matches the PDFs. Photos 2 to 9 name their pages in captions; photo 1 relies on the page title alone. The Print map photo shows every row.

The back of the Print check has 5 fixes, a Settings that work table, and a last line saying to send an Etsy message with a photo of the sheet. There is no reply-time promise anywhere. The listing, however, does not repeat the fixes, which the brief requires: its Help section only points to the sheet.
The listing names both sizes, 14 months of dated pages, the spare week, and 'Print as many copies for your own use as you like'. The Print map gives sheets per row (4, 6, 5, 6, ... and 82 total).
The product is a plain PDF with no app or account. Each month row is 10 or 12 pages (5 or 6 sheets). Spreads fall on even/odd page pairs, so they face each other in the binder.

After the build_changes, Goals, Important dates and Bills sit under the grid and Notes is on the review page. Weeks have a focus list, habit strip and To do list. Labels are Cormorant italic with Jost body text.

Four numbered steps with Page 3 and Page 5 links. The mid-2027 path ('print the current month's row') is there. The early path does not cover December 2026 buyers: both pages send every buyer before 2027 to the November 2026 row (pp 9 to 20, weeks Oct 26 to Nov 29), so a December buyer prints past weeks.

Front: 6 in and 15 cm rulers (measured true size, 96 px/in), four corner marks at 0.5 in, binding-edge hole guides, a line/dot/fill tone sample and a pen test box. Back: same-way-up check, mirrored corner marks, fix list, Settings that work table and a printer notes box.

Gives the page range and sheets for front pages, Nov and Dec 2026, every month of 2027, the spare week and the whole planner, with a Printed tick box per row and two start boxes. Every row starts on an odd page and ends on an even one, so each row is whole sheets.

visual.issue: The start path misroutes December 2026 buyers. Start here step 3 ('Buying in October to December 2026? Print Head start November next') and the Print map box 'Starting before 2027' send every pre-2027 buyer to the November 2026 row, pages 9 to 20 (Oct 26 to Nov 29). A buyer in December who follows the printed steps prints 6 sheets of past weeks and is never told to print December (pages 21 to 30).

Print map rows hold weeks by their Thursday, but no row shows its week dates, so 'print the current month's row' and 'print each row a few days before that month begins' miss the current week near month ends. On Sat May 1, 2027, the May row starts May 3 and the current week (Apr 26) is in April. The July row starts Mon Jun 28, so printing it 'a few days before July' on Jun 29 or 30 loses days. Same for Oct 1 to 3, 2027 and others.

Week numbers are one above ISO 8601 all year. Week 1 is Dec 28 to Jan 3 (ISO 2026-W53), Week 12 is Mar 15 to 21 (ISO W11), and there is a Week 53 although ISO 2027 has 52 weeks. Monday-start and A4 buyers who use work or school week numbers will see mismatched numbers, and nothing explains the scheme.

visual.issue: No photo shows the product as printed paper. Photos 2 to 9 are rounded-corner floating cards with drop shadows and visible on-screen link buttons (Turn over, Page 3, Month review, Thursday to Sunday), so they read as screen or app UI. No photo shows a printed, punched sheet or a binder. Photo 1 is a flat open-book spread with a gutter shadow, not punched sheets in a binder as the brief planned. There are no tablet frames.

The habit name write-in column is only about 0.75 in wide (about 22% of the Habits box, against about 40% in the spec), too narrow to write a habit name by hand. The seven circle columns take the rest.
visual.where: w12b, w01b, hsw01b, spareb (every right page)

visual.issue: Photo 8 shrinks the whole Start here page to fit, so the step text is about 20 px on a 2700 px photo and unreadable at Etsy zoom (r013). The brief also planned the cover in this photo; it is not shown.
Step 2 prints pages 3 to 4, then step 3 and the Print map say 'Print pages 1 to 8 once', which prints the check sheet a second time and wastes a sheet. Saying 1 to 2 and 5 to 8 would avoid it.

The manual duplex instruction ('print odd pages, put the stack back in the tray, then print even pages') does not say which way to reload the stack or whether to reverse the order, which is the usual failure. The back of the check sheet would catch it, but only after a wasted sheet.

Header arrows with no label sit next to labelled links ('<-  Thursday to Sunday ->' on left pages, '<- Monday to Wednesday  ->' on right pages); on paper they read as stray glyphs. Dark filled on-screen pills (cover Start here, Page 3, Page 5, 'Starting in 2026? Head start') print as heavy solid ink blocks.
